scope: A separate public request intake page at canonical /request-ai-access records requests for manual operator review only. It issues no access token, changes no authentication or AI enablement, and grants no workspace authority. The existing workbench is unaffected.
default_and_configuration: OFF by default: blank allow.access-request.config. Explicit enablement requires its absolute path to an external protected JSON file mode 0600 under an owner-trusted 0700 directory, outside the installation, with trusted ancestors. Closed keys are smtpHost, smtpPort, smtpUsername, smtpPassword, sender, siteKey, captchaSecret, hostname and queueDirectory. Queue is a separate existing owner-trusted 0700 directory with trusted ancestors. Service instance optional access_request_config passes only the path, never secrets in argv, environment or package. Validate every value and all paths before enabling; failure is closed. Secrets are externally provisioned, never committed or returned to the browser. Actual configuration and deployment acceptance remain OPEN.
routes: Expose only exact public GET /api/ai-access/config, POST /api/ai-access/challenge and POST /api/ai-access/verify when enabled. Exact canonical paths, no query parameters or Authorization, exact configured Host and mandatory exact same-origin checks on POST; deny Origin null; reject unknown fields, methods, malformed JSON and oversized bodies. GET returns only enabled status and public site key. POST JSON bodies at most 8192 UTF-8 bytes; closed responses and no-store. No workspace identifiers or capabilities are accepted or passed.
page: Separate canonical /request-ai-access main form has a self-only CSP and loads no Google scripts or resources. A captcha-only iframe at exact /request-ai-access/captcha.html uses HTML sandbox allow-scripts only and an HTTP CSP sandbox allow-scripts as well, including on direct navigation. Neither permits forms, popups, top navigation or same-origin. Child CSP frame-ancestors 'self' permits its intended parent and only the child CSP permits minimum Google reCAPTCHA resources. The child receives only the public site key and nonce; no applicant PII, bearer, workspace identifier or authority is supplied. Parent accepts only a closed postMessage schema from the exact iframe event.source with opaque event.origin null and an unpredictable cryptorandom 256-bit nonce rotated on reset, and strict message kinds and token-length bounds; iframe checks exact parent origin, source, nonce and closed schema. Prevent unexpected navigation and reject all other messages. Live Google compatibility with this sandbox is OPEN until configured keys and a human browser test establish it; no unsafe same-origin or parent-script fallback. If incompatible, a separately reviewed dedicated origin is a future option. Do not store request data or code in localStorage or sessionStorage. Render server and provider text inertly. Initial form requires name 1..100 characters, ASCII email 1..254 bytes, optional organization at most 160 characters, purpose 20..2000 characters and explicit acknowledgement. Validate on server; use a bounded strict email syntax and normalize consistently for cooldown keys. Reject control characters and unknown fields.
captcha: Challenge POST carries the complete validated form and one reCAPTCHA token. Consume the token once with HTTPS POST to fixed https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api/siteverify, no redirects, bounded timeout and response body. Require successful HTTP and valid bounded JSON, success exactly true, exact configured hostname, and parseable challenge timestamp no older than two minutes and no more than 30 seconds in the future. Invalid, malformed, timeout, provider outage or any uncertainty fails closed. Do not log token, response or applicant fields.
verification: After successful captcha, bind the immutable complete validated form to an unpredictable 256-bit challenge and independently generated cryptographically random unbiased eight-digit email code. Store only a salted code hash in bounded process memory; no plaintext code after send. TTL 10 minutes, at most five code attempts. Restart invalidates all challenges. Verify POST accepts exactly challenge and code, never applicant fields; it completes the same immutable request without another captcha. Check expiry before final durable persistence. Successful persistence atomically consumes the challenge under synchronization; duplicate, expired, exhausted and replayed verification fail closed. Never send an accepted receipt on persistence failure.
limits: At most 100 live in-memory challenges; bounded per-email state. At most 10 global captcha/email challenge attempts per hour, per-email cooldown 60 seconds and at most three per hour; verify at most 60 globally per minute. At most two network operations concurrently across captcha and SMTP; deny when full. Reserve limits before external work, including failures; enforce atomically. Rates are single-process and restart resets them; a durable independent edge rate limiter is a required production gate for restart and distributed abuse and cost exposure.
mail: Send verification code only through authenticated SMTP with mandatory STARTTLS and hostname validation; connect, read and write timeouts each at most five seconds, fixed configured sender and bounded message. Fail closed on any error. Never log raw exceptions, SMTP replies, credentials, code, captcha token or applicant PII. Do not send actual email during development or acceptance without explicit operator provisioning. Fixed plaintext message contains only the code, its TTL and site; never applicant name or purpose.
queue: Durable pending records only; no SQL. External owner-trusted directory mode 0700, reject symlinks and insecure ownership/permissions. Write each bounded record as a create-new random UUID file mode 0600, with no overwrite and at most 1000 retained records. Durable completion requires successful write and flush to stable storage including directory entry; ambiguity fails closed. Synchronize capacity, final expiry, fsync commit before consumption, and consumption to avoid duplicate records. Retain records for 30 days and document explicit operator purge thereafter; never automatically approve or issue tokens.
proof_scope: Finite abstract policy only: admission requires captcha, email verification, live unconsumed challenge, current immutable binding, remaining attempts and persistence; consumption closes replay and no token is generated. Clock, randomness, serializer, concurrency, SMTP, Google, filesystem, deployment and refinement to implementation are trusted and unproved.
acceptance_open: External configuration and secrets, actual SMTP/Google/hostname/queue provisioning, delivery, operational review workflow, production deployment and commercial acceptance remain OPEN. Operator must assess provider terms, pricing, message volume, spam and abuse costs and independent edge limits before enablement. Formal and council evidence precede production changes.
